Beat 1: **Severe childhood asthma kept him indoors, so he watched the world through a window and reinvented cinema.**

Beat 2: Born November 17, 1942, Martin Scorsese turns 84 today, originating from Queens, New York.

Beat 3: Too sickly to play sports in Little Italy, he spent childhood inside movie theaters and studied to become a Catholic priest.

Beat 4: Pivoting to NYU Film School, he brought raw street energy, kinetic editing, and rock-and-roll soundtracks to American cinema.

Beat 5: Directing Taxi Driver, Raging Bull, and Goodfellas, he forged cinema's greatest partnerships with Robert De Niro and Leonardo DiCaprio.

Beat 6: Enduring decades of painful Oscar snubs despite creating generational masterpieces, he finally won Best Director for The Departed.

Beat 7: Delivering The Wolf of Wall Street and Killers of the Flower Moon, he stands as cinema's living master.

Beat 8: **Is Goodfellas, Taxi Driver, or The Departed Martin Scorsese's greatest cinematic masterpiece?**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind cinema's greatest living auteur:**
• Attended a Catholic preparatory seminary in New York before enrolling at New York University's film school.
• Won the Academy Award for Best Director for The Departed in 2007 after five previous directing nominations.
• Founded The Film Foundation in 1990, helping restore and preserve over nine hundred classic films worldwide.

Which masterpiece sits at the top of his filmography: Goodfellas or The Wolf of Wall Street?
posts.reel_script: Before directing Goodfellas, Taxi Driver, and The Departed, a young boy in New York suffered from severe asthma that kept him off the playground and inside dark movie theaters. First studying to enter the Catholic priesthood, he pivoted to NYU Film School and unleashed raw, kinetic storytelling that changed cinema forever. Still creating masterpieces at eighty-four, he is a living legend. Happy birthday! Which of his films is your favorite?
